# Catalog

* [Seams, stitches and allowances](seams-stitches-and-allowances.md) - Industrial stitch types, densities, threads and needles for this fabric class, home/atelier equivalents, thread-colour rules, and seam and hem allowances (6 mm on body seams almost universally).

# Design Rule

* [Rule: crystal keep-outs and machine limits](rule-crystal-keep-outs.md) - Manufacturability checks for stones: keep-out bands at seams, elastic edges and layered areas, underarm exclusion, small stones on straps, separate glue footprints, setter field and hopper limits, and test flags for foil and metallic bases.
* [Rule: decoration crossing seams](rule-decoration-crossing-seams.md) - Because decoration is applied to flat pieces before the side, shoulder and crotch seams are closed, any print, appliqué or crystal motif crossing a seam must be split per piece or finished by hand after assembly.
* [Rule: grain, nap and fabric assignment](rule-grain-nap-and-fabric-assignment.md) - Greatest stretch runs around the body on every structural piece (straps and long narrow appliqués excepted), napped and one-way fabrics are cut one way, and low-stretch fabrics are flagged on structural panels.
* [Rule: heat-process order](rule-heat-process-order.md) - Recommended heat order is sublimation (about 190-230 C), then vinyl or foil transfers (about 130-160 C), then hotfix crystals (about 160-170 C); the bands overlap, so flag any process that would exceed the tolerance of a layer already applied.
* [Rule: lining](rule-lining.md) - Competition leotards are front-lined or fully lined and always crotch-lined; lining is bonded to the shell and sewn as one layer, in nude tones, and is required under light, sublimated white-base and revealing fabrics.
* [Rule: mesh use](rule-mesh-use.md) - Mesh panels need a lining or self-backing decision, colour-matched elastic and thread, a 1 in overlap where they back a cut-out, and warnings in contact and abrasion zones; mesh carries no durability guarantee at GK.
* [Rule: openings and straps](rule-openings-and-straps.md) - Checks for necklines, keyholes, cut-outs and strap layouts: Porter's spacing and width formulas, step-in size and closure, elastic or binding on every opening, and dress-code limits.
* [Rule: pieced seam geometry](rule-pieced-seam-geometry.md) - Lines realised as pieced seams must be straight or gently curved with no inside corners or L-insets, panels must be wider than their allowances, and seam count and seam placement in strain zones are limited; thresholds are factory-set defaults.
* [What makes a pattern true](what-makes-a-pattern-true.md) - The checks every block and design must pass before its flat pieces are trusted, why the mesh may never be the source of an outline, and what the first run found: the owner's three visible defects were our processing, while the bought block has faults of its own at the high leg, crotch, sleeve and curve resolution.

# Domain Concept

* [Appliqué and overlays](applique-and-overlays.md) - How appliqué, reverse appliqué, padded appliqué, mesh-backed cut-outs, heat-transfer vinyl and foil are made on stretch leotards, and what an appliqué export must contain.
* [Back, strap and keyhole formulas](back-strap-and-keyhole-formulas.md) - Encodable atelier formulas for strappy backs, keyholes, strap cut widths and banded collars, in inches with metric equivalents, plus the dress-code limits that constrain backs.
* [The purchased leotard block (BasicPatternBlock 0005)](basicpatternblock-leotard-block.md) - What the block bought on 2026-11-01 contains and measures: an unlocked true-scale vector PDF with a layer per size, three pieces, two leg cuts and two sleeve lengths, seams that match within 0.5 mm, and negative ease that varies by height and size.
* [One look, several builds](builds-for-one-look.md) (draft) - A mesh bodice carrying opaque plates can be built at least four ways (seam enclosed by lining, window from behind, plate on a whole base, plate under the mesh), and a photo rarely shows which; what is cut and what shows through differ even when the picture does not.
* [Clothing pressure and comfort](clothing-pressure-comfort.md) (draft) - Published comfort limits for garment pressure on the body (swimsuits, leotards, girdles, sports compression): about 0.5-1 kPa (4-7.5 mmHg) is comfortable on the trunk, about 2 kPa (15 mmHg) tolerated at straps and waistbands, about 4 kPa (30 mmHg, near capillary pressure) too tight anywhere; usable to flag tightness from the fit solver's strain.
* [Three ways to make a design line](design-line-realisations.md) - Every line a designer draws becomes a pieced seam (straight or gentle curves, 6 mm allowances), a stitched appliqué overlay (any shape, extra layer), or a sublimated print boundary (no seam); the choice sets the line's shape limits and cost.
* [DXF pattern exchange](dxf-pattern-exchange.md) - DXF-AAMA (often R10/R12-style) is the practical pattern interchange format in 2026, DXF-ASTM (ASTM D6673, withdrawn 2019) is supported but loosely defined, and imports break on layers, notches, seam-allowance/cut-line confusion and units.
* [Edge finishing: elastic and binding](edge-finishing-elastic-and-binding.md) - Leg, neck and arm openings are finished with about 1 cm (3/8 in) elastic turned and topstitched, or with a binding strip; elastic is cut shorter than the opening by rules that range from 0% to 25%.
* [Factory deliverables](factory-deliverables.md) - What a design must become for a factory or seamstress to act on it: DXF pattern pieces with markings, plot files, per-piece print images, per-piece stone maps and counts, appliqué pieces, and a tech pack with BOM, graded spec and construction notes.
* [What factory footage shows of leotard patterns](factory-pattern-footage.md) (draft) - Four frames from old behind-the-scenes videos (GK Elite, about 2010; Alpha Factor via FloGymnastics, 2016): patterns are drafted in CAD as corner and curve points with internal lines and alternative curves on one piece, and cut from nested markers by size; Alpha Factor's body pieces appear cut full width with both leg openings rather than on a fold. Little on drafting itself.
* [Fit failures in wear](fit-failures-in-wear.md) (draft) - How leotards fail on a moving body according to reviews and swimwear fit guides (seat ride-up, tight armholes, straps digging or slipping, leg line migrating, floating neckline) with the stated cause and pattern correction; torso length is the most-named root cause.
* [Grading across sizes](grading-across-sizes.md) - How leotard patterns change between sizes: torso (girth) grades about 3 in per child size and 0.5-3 in per adult size depending on brand, long/short torso is a one-size length grade, trims are graded too, and each manufacturer needs its own grade table.
* [Negative ease](negative-ease.md) - Leotard pieces are cut smaller than the body; published reductions range from 0-10% to about 15-22% of width and 0-11% of length, there is no standard, and the figure must be set per fabric (and so per panel).
* [Pattern markings](pattern-markings.md) - What a leotard pattern piece must carry besides its outline: cut and sew lines, notches (and their types), grain/stretch line, fold/mirror line, internal lines, cut-outs, drill holes, piece labels, and how each maps to DXF layers in the two known conventions.
* [Patternmaking texts for stretch and leotards](patternmaking-texts-for-stretch.md) (draft) - Drafting methods beyond Armstrong that we may follow and restate (methods, not blocks, so the results are ours): Aldrich women's (6th ed. 2015, close-fitting stretch ch. 13) and children's (4th ed. 2009, sport and leisurewear ch. 7), Haggar's lingerie and beachwear (2nd ed. 2004), Porter's Sewing for Gymnasts; Shin is bra-focused; no former-GK patternmaker source exists publicly.
* [Sources of leotard pattern blocks](sources-of-leotard-pattern-blocks.md) - Where a flat leotard pattern can come from as ground truth, as read on 2026-11-01: no tool found ships a preloaded leotard block library; BasicPatternBlock's unlocked block has the clearest terms, FreeSewing Onyx is a free measurement-driven generator, and Browzwear's cloud has ungraded swimwear blocks.
* [Stretch block drafting and alterations](stretch-block-drafting.md) - How a leotard block is measured, drafted, altered for necklines and backs, split into colour-block panels, and how stretch sleeves differ; the atelier procedures the pattern tool must reproduce.
* [Watkins stretch-reduction method](watkins-stretch-reduction-method.md) - The one published quantitative method for turning measured fabric stretch into separate width and length pattern scale factors, with its quad-load stretch test; the documented default for per-fabric negative ease.

# Open Question

* [Open question: unpublished factory pattern data](open-question-factory-pattern-data.md) (draft) - No leotard manufacturer publishes its block, negative ease, garment measurements, seam and stitch spec, manufacturability thresholds, CAD system or file requirements; these must come from conversations with one or two target manufacturers.
* [Open question: stoning state and crystal grading across sizes](open-question-stoning-state-and-crystal-grading.md) (draft) - Are stones applied to relaxed flat pieces or to stretched fabric, and how do makers carry a crystal layout across sizes (keep count or keep spacing)? Both decide which spacing check binds and how layouts grade.

# Process

* [Aldrich's stretch body, bodyshaper and swimwear blocks](aldrich-stretch-body-and-swimwear-blocks.md) (draft) - What Aldrich's Women's Wear (5th ed., 2008) teaches for close-fitting stretch: a metric, measurement-driven leotard-shaped block (bodyshaper and swimwear) with fixed-centimetre reductions that work out to about 16-21% at the bust, 5-7% at the waist and 11-15% at the low waist, no length reduction, an ease ladder from negative to +4 cm, point grade rules, and a fault-to-correction table; restated in our own words with implied percentages.
* [Armstrong leotard and bodysuit foundation drafts](armstrong-leotard-foundation-draft.md) (draft) - Joseph-Armstrong's textbook method for drafting a stretch leotard (and full bodysuit) foundation from a basic back bodice plus three to six body measurements; the candidate route to blocks the project owns outright.
* [Custom-order process, lead times and prices](custom-order-process-and-lead-times.md) - Every maker runs custom team orders as brief, digital design with revisions, sign-off, sizing kit, production; lead times run 2 to 13 weeks and embellishment is the main price driver.
* [Cutting and marker making](cutting-and-marker-making.md) - Factories spread and laser-cut layered stretch fabric and bundle by athlete size; ateliers cut single garments by hand; a one-colour leotard uses about 0.5-1.35 m of 150 cm fabric.
* [Production and assembly order](production-and-assembly-order.md) - Factories cut, print, appliqué, embroider and stone flat pieces, then close side, shoulder and crotch seams last; ateliers and home makers follow related but different sewing orders.
* [Yardsticks from real leotards](real-leotard-yardsticks.md) (draft) - How we check that our own drafted blocks match real competition leotards without anyone's blocks: flat garment measurements (owner-measured and resale listings), construction evidence, fit failures in wear and comfort pressure; first resale numbers suggest about 16-27% chest and 8-24% length reduction on GK.
* [Sublimation production](sublimation-production.md) - Sublimated artwork is engineered per pattern piece and per size, printed mirrored on paper and transferred at about 190-230 C for 30-60 s, either onto cut pieces (GK) or onto the roll before laser cutting; what this means for per-piece print files.
